problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & {t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & {t}^{2} \\ 2 & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,4{t}^{2}-2{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,2{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+({t}^{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{t}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(4+{t}^{2})} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{1}+(0)^{2}+(2{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
